Kazimierz Dolny Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kazimierz Dolny, Poland

Demolished. First Jewish records in Kazimierz Dolny date to 1406, and in the 19th century the town became the seat of the Kuzmir Hasidic dynasty, founded by Rebbe Jechezkiel Taub. This cemetery, established in the 16th century and first documented in 1588, was ordered closed in 1792 in favor of a new burial site outside the city — though that new cemetery wasn't actually established until 1851, and sporadic burials continued here in the meantime, including that of Rebbe Taub himself in 1856. German forces ordered part of the cemetery hill leveled during WWII and built barracks on the site; a school and playground followed in the 1950s or 1960s, with fragments of matzevot used to build a retaining wall for the playground. Bones periodically slide out of the leveled hillside even today, and recent archaeological work has confirmed many graves lie beneath the playground itself. This record's gravestone-count field reads '1980' — implausibly high for a site that is 90 percent overbuilt with only a few small tombstone fragments surviving, and likely another instance of a data-entry mix-up rather than a genuine count, matching a pattern flagged elsewhere in this collection. Unlike several other Polish cemeteries in this collection, this site carries no formal heritage-registry listing.
